title: Count the Roof Beasts: Only One Building in China Has 10 | China Travel Expert
description:
On a Chinese palace roof, a little parade of glazed animals rides each corner ridge — and the number isn't decoration, it's rank. The more figures a hall is allowed, the higher its status. For almost every building, nine is the ceiling.

Only one roof in all of Chinese architecture breaks it: the Hall of Supreme Harmony (Taihedian) in Beijing's Forbidden City, the emperor's throne hall. It carries a tenth figure — Hangshi, a winged, monkey-faced guardian — that appears on no other roof in the country. So if you're ever standing in the Forbidden City, look up and count: on every other hall you'll stop at nine or fewer.

★ Expert Tip: the figures always follow the same order behind the rider up front — dragon, phoenix, lion, and so on — so once you learn the line-up you can read any roof's rank from the ground.

中国古建筑屋脊上的走兽数量代表等级，一般最多九个；唯有故宫太和殿用到十个，第十个"行什"别处再无。
